Before you buy a rural Caledon home, read this. 1) Ask for a recent water test, and test the well yourself. 2) Ask how old the well and septic system are. 3) Ask for septic records, like pumping and past repairs. 4) Book a specialist inspection; a general one may not cover them. Save this before your Caledon home search.

First home in Waterloo Region? 2 programs worth knowing. 1) Ontario land transfer tax refund: eligible first-time buyers may get back up to $4,000 (Source: Ontario.ca, checked Oct 2026). 2) First Home Savings Account: up to $8,000 a year, $40,000 lifetime limit; contributions may be tax-deductible and qualifying first-home withdrawals are tax-free (Source: Canada Revenue Agency, checked Oct 2026). Each program has its own eligibility rules. Save this and send it to someone buying their first home.

Buying a condo in Etobicoke? Read the status certificate first. It shows things like the reserve fund, monthly fees, any special assessments and legal issues involving the condo corporation. Ask your lawyer to review it.

Home inspections: 3 things nobody tells you. 1) It is usually a condition of your offer, with a deadline. 2) Attend if you can; you learn more than the report shows. 3) Ask which items are urgent and which can wait. Send this to someone buying their first home.
